speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the patient experienced any seizures, loss of consciousness, or changes in speech lately?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain shows disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis

The MRI confirms the presence of disseminated white matter lesions consistent with demyelination, which explains the combination of motor weakness, gait instability, and cognitive changes. While the paranoid behavior is less typical, it can occur due to frontal lobe involvement in advanced or atypical cases. Given the 6-month duration of cognitive decline alongside the recent onset of motor symptoms, this pattern strongly supports a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis.
